title: Restricted Content Discovery: how do you keep a SharePoint site out of Copilot and organisation-wide search?
summary: The licensing requirements, site setting, delegation command and reporting commands are supported by Microsoft documentation. The statement that a restriction hides a site from Copilot indefinitely needs narrowing, and the page should acknowledge conflicting Microsoft descriptions of recent-interaction exceptions and the setting label.

claims.where: summary; What it is; controls[0].scope
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level SharePoint setting.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting.

claims.where: summary; What it is; controls[0].governs
claims.claim: The setting limits discovery of site content, including recently interacted files, in organisation-wide search and Microsoft Copilot responses.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery helps you limit discovery of content from specific SharePoint sites, including recently interacted files, in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses while those reviews are taking place.
claims.fix: Add: 'Microsoft's Restricted Content Discovery page includes recently interacted files, but https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/manage/copilot-search-manage describes an exception for content a user owns or recently interacted with, and https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/sharepoint-advanced-management-features-copilot-license describes a recent-interaction exception for Copilot Business Chat.' Do not resolve the disagreement by silently choosing either description.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Restricted Content Discovery page publishes no separate price or meter for the setting as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Restricted Content Discovery" "price" "meter". Read https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/restricted-content-discovery and the SAM prerequisites in full; neither publishes a separate RCD price or meter.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Copilot licence pricing is published on Microsoft's pricing and licensing resources, not on the Restricted Content Discovery page.
claims.quote: Before you purchase or assign licenses, confirm eligibility in the Microsoft Product Terms, Microsoft Copilot service description, and Microsoft Copilot pricing and plans.
claims.fix: Add the Microsoft pages relied on but missing from sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/microsoft-365-copilot-licensing, https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/pricing/business, https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/manage/copilot-search-manage and https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/sharepoint-advanced-management-features-copilot-license. The licensing page links to pricing and plans, and the pricing page publishes per-user subscription prices; the other two pages document the recent-interaction exceptions that should be acknowledged.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Temporary by design
claims.claim: A restriction left in place after review hides the site from Copilot indefinitely.
claims.quote: Searched: "Restricted Content Discovery" "expire". Read the RCD page in full and results for Manage access to agents in SharePoint and Catalog management. No passage states an indefinite duration; the RCD page also exempts content already in use.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet's sentence with: 'After the review is complete, you can remove the restriction and allow the sites to become discoverable again.' This is stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/restricted-content-discovery.

claims.where: controls[0].ui
claims.claim: The setting is at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites.
Select the site you want to configure.
Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.
claims.fix: Keep the documented path, but add to controls[0].note: 'The Copilot readiness guide instead labels the setting Restrict content discovery > On on the same Settings tab.' The differing label is at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/get-ready-copilot-sharepoint-advanced-management.

claims.where: controls[0].api
claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables the site's restriction.
claims.quote:
For any parameters that are passed in, the Set-SPOSite cmdlet sets or updates the setting for the site collection identified by parameter Identity.
-RestrictContentOrgWideSearch
Type: System.Boolean
claims.fix: Keep the command, which the RCD page explicitly gives, but add: 'The Set-SPOSite reference's valid-parameter list for Groups site collections omits RestrictContentOrgWideSearch, whereas the Restricted Content Discovery guide gives this command without that qualification.' Both pages are already cited.

Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $false
